```{python}
# Read in the names data
```

## Question 1:

### Recreate the following graph

Note: graph is different due to different year being used to calculate age
```{python}
# Question 1 Code

# How old is someone named Russell?
# x - Age
# y - Frequency
# Geom point(?) on Russell M. Nelson

print(names)
print(names.schema)

# Filter out Russell and remove states
russell_df = (names
  .select("name", "year", "Total")
  .filter(pl.col("name") == "Russell")
)

russell_df.head()
```

```{python}

# Calculate ages (based on current year)
russell_df = (russell_df
  .with_columns(
    age = 2026 - (pl.col("year").cast(pl.Int32))
  )
)

russell_df.head()

```

```{python}
# Make graph
plot_df = (russell_df
  .select("Total", "age")
  .with_columns(
    Total = pl.col("Total").cast(pl.Float16).cast(pl.Int32)
  )
)

plot_df
```

```{python}
# Make graph
# How old is someone named Russell?
# x - Age
# y - Frequency
# Geom point(?) on Russell M. Nelson

# Not the best on theme stuff so this is my best shot
(
ggplot(plot_df, aes("age", "Total"))
+ geom_line(color="red", size=2)
+ geom_point(x=100, y=3900, color="blue", size=7)
+ geom_text(x=100, y=4500, label="Russell M. Nelson")
+ scale_x_continuous(limits=[0, 120])
+ scale_y_continuous(limits=[0, 8000])
+ labs(
  "How old is someone named Russell?",
  x = "Age",
  y = "Frequency"
)
)

```
